title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Nvidia Wipeout, Then a Long Paddle Back
conditions.summary: Stocks slipped as Nvidia's CEO resigned and rising Fed rate-hike odds pushed the 10-year yield back above 5 percent. The S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq each fell 0.4 percent after clawing back an early drop, while small caps lost 1.7 percent.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 fell 26.98 points, or 0.4%, to 7,592.40.
The Dow lost 189.40 points, or 0.4%, to 52,297.09, and the Nasdaq fell 100.10 points, or 0.4%, to 25,366.09.
Small caps took the hardest hit: the Russell 2000 dropped 1.7% to 2,799.06.
The S&P 500 was down nearly 1% at the open after Nvidia's CEO resigned, erased the loss by midday, then drifted lower into the close.
Rising odds of a December Fed rate hike weighed on growth stocks; early in the day energy led and technology lagged.
The VIX fear gauge rose 6.9% to 18.70. Even after today, the S&P 500 is up 2.9% for the week.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: Initial jobless claims rose to 200,000, above the 195,000 forecast.
Existing-home sales fell to a 3.75 million annual pace in October, below the 3.85 million forecast and the weakest since 2010.
Markets now price about a 94% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate hike at the December 9 meeting.
Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said inflation pressures are broadening and favored steady, smaller hikes.
The 10-year Treasury yield climbed back above 5%, and the dollar index rose above 103.
Oil jumped after President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran; WTI settled at $88.74, up 2.6%.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: NVDA (Nvidia): about -6% — CEO Jensen Huang resigned effectively immediately; shares fell as much as 14% early before recovering about half.
AVGO (Broadcom): +5.5% — chip rivals rallied amid Nvidia's leadership turmoil.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): +5.3% — an analyst upgrade plus bets it can gain ground on Nvidia.
ANET (Arista Networks): +4.6% — AI networking names caught a bid.
SMCI (Super Micro Computer): about -10% — slid with AI hardware stocks.
BABA (Alibaba): about -7% — reports US regulators may restrict remote access to advanced AI chips.
LCID (Lucid): -11.0% and ACHR (Archer Aviation): -11.1% — speculative names sold off as yields rose.
IONQ (IonQ): -9.5% — quantum stocks lost altitude with other high-flyers.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Applied Materials reported after the close: revenue of $10.41 billion, up 53% from a year ago, and adjusted EPS of $4.16, topping estimates.
Applied Materials gave upbeat guidance and shares rose about 1.4% after hours.
Nebius reported third-quarter revenue up more than fivefold from a year ago, but the shares fell.
Nvidia says it still plans to report quarterly results on November 17.

sections.title: Business News
items: Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO and director Harvey Jones as board chair after Jensen Huang stepped down.
President Trump posted that Apple CEO Tim Cook should run Nvidia; neither company said Cook is under consideration.
MSCI will drop Strategy, the big bitcoin holder, from its global indexes after the November 30 close.
CoreWeave is lining up at least a $4 billion investment-grade loan.
Pfizer and Blackstone agreed on $1.5 billion of co-funding for obesity drug work.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Friday 7:30 AM CT: October Producer Price Index, a key read on inflation after this week's hot CPI.
Tuesday, Nov. 17: Nvidia earnings and October retail sales.
Wednesday, Nov. 18, 1:00 PM CT: minutes from the Fed's October meeting.
December 9: Fed decision, with a rate hike nearly fully priced in.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Thursday, November twelfth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down into the water, the last set is rolling in, and it was a gnarly one. Gus the wonder dog is back on the deck after a long day of chasing sand crabs. Say good evening, Gus! Here's the final set. The S and P five hundred slipped four tenths of a percent to seven thousand five hundred ninety two. The Dow also lost four tenths of a percent, to fifty two thousand two hundred ninety seven. The Nasdaq fell four tenths of a percent to twenty five thousand three hundred sixty six. Small caps took the real wipeout, with the Russell two thousand down one point seven percent. The big story broke before the opening bell. Nvidia said Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is the interim boss. Nvidia dropped as much as fourteen percent early, then paddled back about half of that, ending down around six percent. Now the wind and weather. Rates were the other headwind. Traders now see about a ninety four percent chance the Fed hikes a quarter point on December ninth. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said inflation pressures are broadening. The ten year Treasury yield pushed back above five percent, and the dollar index rose above one hundred three. Existing home sales sank to their slowest pace since twenty ten. Oil jumped two point six percent after President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran. Gold fell about three percent, and bitcoin dropped below seventy two thousand dollars. Over in the lineup, Nvidia's rivals were stoked. Broadcom rode that swell all the way to the beach, up five and a half percent. Gus, that one's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Advanced Micro Devices gained five percent after an analyst upgrade, and Arista Networks added four and a half. On the wipeout side, Super Micro Computer fell about ten percent, and Alibaba lost about seven on reports of new limits on remote access to A I chips. Lucid and Archer Aviation each dropped about eleven percent. Speculative high flyers looked like hodads today once yields started climbing. On the tide chart, Applied Materials reported after the bell. Revenue jumped fifty three percent to ten point four billion dollars, profit topped estimates, and the shares rose about one percent after hours. Nvidia still plans to report on Tuesday the seventeenth. Some beach talk. M S C I will drop Strategy, the big bitcoin holder, from its global indexes at the end of the month. And CoreWeave is lining up a loan of at least four billion dollars. Tomorrow's forecast. The producer price index lands at seven thirty A M Central, a key inflation check after this week's hot consumer price report. Soul surfers, remember the S and P is still up almost three percent this week, so no need to panic over one choppy afternoon. Wax that board and catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning.
